messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (`storage/<env>.sqlite3`), Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus via Importmap), and Propshaft for local assets. All design assets (`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2`) are served locally without external network dependencies.

## Runtime & Deployment

- `bin/serve` prepares `storage/`, runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` (`RAILS_ENV=production` by default).
- Production runs over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`) and accepts any `Host` header (`config.hosts.clear`).
- `GET /up` serves the unauthenticated Rails health check (`200 OK`).
- All persistent data lives under `storage/`.

## Authentication

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using constant-time SHA-256 digest comparison (`ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`). Empty/missing env vars reject with `401`.
- The moderator layout sets `<meta name="turbo-cache-control" content="no-cache">` so Turbo Drive never flashes stale cached forms or stale database state during navigation.

## Data Model

- `Quiz` (`quizzes`: `title`) `has_many :questions, dependent: :destroy`
- `Question` (`questions`: `quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active`) `has_many :options, dependent: :destroy`
- `Option` (`options`: `question_id`, `body`, `correct`, `position`)

## Export & Import

- `Quiz::Exporter` (`app/models/quiz/exporter.rb`) serializes a quiz to pretty-printed JSON with **strictly** these keys:
  - Top-level: `title`, `questions`
  - Each question (in `position, id` order): `text`, `active` (boolean, always present), `options`
  - Each option (in `position, id` order): `text`, `correct` (boolean, always present)
  - Future releases adding live runs, participants, settings, or timestamps must **not** add extra keys to the export format; export is strictly for moving quiz contents.
- `Quiz::Importer` (`app/models/quiz/importer.rb`) validates the JSON syntax, types, and question rules (non-blank title, non-blank question/option text, optional `active` defaulting to `true`, optional `correct` defaulting to `false`, strict booleans when present, at least 2 options per question, at least 1 correct option per question) before creating a brand new `Quiz` and all its questions/options atomically inside a single database transaction.
- Routes:
  - `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/export` (`Moderate::ExportsController#show`) renders the JSON inside the single `<pre>` element on the page.
  - `GET /moderate/import` (`Moderate::ImportsController#new`) and `POST /moderate/import` (`Moderate::ImportsController#create`) render and process the "Quiz JSON" import form.

### Notes for Future Releases (Live Runs & Audience Play)

- Currently, editing a question replaces its `options` atomically inside a transaction (`Question#save_with_option_rows`). Once future releases add live game runs and participant answers referencing `option_id` (or snapshotting questions/options per run), either snapshot questions/options when a run starts or update existing options in place by ID to preserve foreign keys.
- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` already contains styling tokens and components for big-screen presentation (`.screen`, `.stage-options`, `.leaderboard`, `.lobby`, `.qr`), participant mobile play (`.play`, `.play-options`, `.play-status`, `.result-card`), and moderator run history (`.runs-table`, `.response-options`).
- ActionCable is currently configured with the `async` adapter in `config/cable.yml` (sufficient for single-process Puma). If multi-worker Puma is ever enabled, switch to `solid_cable` storing its SQLite database under `storage/`.
- Preview (`Moderate::PreviewsController#show` + `preview_controller.js`) runs entirely in client memory from the active questions JSON payload and stores no answers in the database, cookies, or web storage.

### Notes for Future Releases (Live Runs & Audience Play)

- Currently, editing a question replaces its `options` atomically inside a transaction (`Question#save_with_option_rows`). Once future releases add live game runs and participant answers referencing `option_id` (or snapshotting questions/options per run), either snapshot questions/options when a run starts or update existing options in place by ID to preserve foreign keys.
- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` already contains styling tokens and components for big-screen presentation (`.screen`, `.stage-options`, `.leaderboard`, `.lobby`, `.qr`), participant mobile play (`.play`, `.play-options`, `.play-status`, `.result-card`), and moderator run history (`.runs-table`, `.response-options`).
- ActionCable is currently configured with the `async` adapter in `config/cable.yml` (sufficient for single-process Puma). If multi-worker Puma is ever enabled, switch to `solid_cable` storing its SQLite database under `storage/`.
- Preview (`Moderate::PreviewsController#show` + `preview_controller.js`) runs entirely in client memory from the active questions JSON payload and stores no answers in the database, cookies, or web storage.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  OptionRow = Data.define(:body, :correct)

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }
  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0 }

  before_validation :assign_default_position, on: :create

  def save_with_option_rows(submitted_rows)
    normalized_rows = Array(submitted_rows).map do |row|
      if row.is_a?(OptionRow)
        row
      else
        OptionRow.new(
          body: (row[:body] || row["body"]).to_s,
          correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct] || row["correct"]) || false
        )
      end
    end

    filled_rows = normalized_rows.reject { |row| row.body.strip.empty? }

    valid_self = valid?

    if filled_rows.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options")
    elsif filled_rows.none?(&:correct)
      errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct")
    end

    return false unless valid_self && errors.empty?

    transaction do
      save!
      options.destroy_all
      filled_rows.each_with_index do |row, index|
        options.create!(
          body: row.body.strip,
          correct: row.correct,
          position: index + 1
        )
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move(:up)
  end

  def move_down!
    move(:down)
  end

  def move(direction)
    quiz.transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      idx = ordered.index(self)
      return unless idx

      target_idx = direction == :up ? idx - 1 : idx + 1
      return if target_idx.negative? || target_idx >= ordered.size

      ordered[idx], ordered[target_idx] = ordered[target_idx], ordered[idx]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        new_pos = i + 1
        question.update_column(:position, new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def assign_default_position
    return if position.present?

    self.position = (quiz&.questions&.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end
end

module Moderate
  class QuestionsController < BaseController
    before_action :set_quiz
    before_action :set_question, only: %i[edit update destroy move_up move_down toggle_active]

    def new
      @question = @quiz.questions.build(active: true)
      @option_rows = Array.new(4) { Question::OptionRow.new(body: "", correct: false) }
    end

    def create
      @question = @quiz.questions.build(question_params)
      @option_rows = submitted_option_rows

      if @question.save_with_option_rows(@option_rows)
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
      else
        render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def edit
      @option_rows = @question.options.ordered.map do |option|
        Question::OptionRow.new(body: option.body, correct: option.correct?)
      end
    end

    def update
      @question.assign_attributes(question_params)
      @option_rows = submitted_option_rows

      if @question.save_with_option_rows(@option_rows)
        redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
      else
        render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity
      end
    end

    def destroy
      @question.destroy!
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    def move_up
      @question.move_up!
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    def move_down
      @question.move_down!
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    def toggle_active
      active = ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(params.dig(:question, :active))
      @question.update!(active: active || false)
      redirect_to moderate_quiz_path(@quiz), status: :see_other
    end

    private

    def set_quiz
      @quiz = Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id])
    end

    def set_question
      @question = @quiz.questions.find(params[:id])
    end

    def question_params
      params.require(:question).permit(:body, :active)
    end

    def submitted_option_rows
      raw = params.dig(:question, :option_rows)
      rows = case raw
      when ActionController::Parameters, Hash
               raw.to_unsafe_h.sort_by { |key, _| key.to_i }.map { |_, value| value }
      when Array
               raw
      else
               []
      end

      rows.map do |row|
        row_hash = row.respond_to?(:to_h) ? row.to_h : {}
        Question::OptionRow.new(
          body: row_hash["body"].to_s,
          correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row_hash["correct"]) || false
        )
      end
    end
  end
end

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  OptionRow = Data.define(:body, :correct)

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }
  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0 }

  before_validation :assign_default_position, on: :create

  def save_with_option_rows(submitted_rows)
    normalized_rows = Array(submitted_rows).map do |row|
      if row.is_a?(OptionRow)
        row
      else
        OptionRow.new(
          body: (row[:body] || row["body"]).to_s,
          correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct] || row["correct"]) || false
        )
      end
    end

    filled_rows = normalized_rows.reject { |row| row.body.strip.empty? }

    valid_self = valid?

    if filled_rows.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options")
    elsif filled_rows.none?(&:correct)
      errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct")
    end

    return false unless valid_self && errors.empty?

    transaction do
      save!
      options.destroy_all
      filled_rows.each_with_index do |row, index|
        options.create!(
          body: row.body.strip,
          correct: row.correct,
          position: index + 1
        )
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move(:up)
  end

  def move_down!
    move(:down)
  end

  def move(direction)
    quiz.transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      idx = ordered.index(self)
      return unless idx

      target_idx = direction == :up ? idx - 1 : idx + 1
      return if target_idx.negative? || target_idx >= ordered.size

      ordered[idx], ordered[target_idx] = ordered[target_idx], ordered[idx]
      ordered.each_with_index do |question, i|
        new_pos = i + 1
        question.update_column(:position, new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def assign_default_position
    return if position.present?

    self.position = (quiz&.questions&.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end
end

      when Array

messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into Quiz Game Requirements**

Okay, first off, the existing tests are reassuringly snappy. Capybara with Cuprite? No issues. Good. Now, let's *really* dig into this prompt. We're talking edge cases, architecture, real-time updates, presence, resilience on conference Wi-Fi (a potential nightmare!), QR code generation, security... the whole nine yards. Let's start with the text and not leave a single stone unturned.

Alright, step one: a complete, thorough re-read of the requirements, and then we will break them down into their component parts to ensure a complete understanding.

Now, that said, the first major concept to deal with is user presence and the implications within the application. Specifically: "players currently waiting for the quiz to start" versus "players currently in the game" - that phrasing is critical. It implies online/connected presence tracking. If a user disconnects, do they remain in the total "waiting" count? Are they removed from the "in the game" count? And what about the conference Wi-Fi scenario?

This "crowded conference Wi-Fi" bit is *huge*. That means flaky connections, dropped packets, and all sorts of chaos. We need to handle WebSocket disconnects gracefully, with seamless reconnection and no data loss. ActionCable seems like a likely candidate, but we need to check how it will perform here. If ActionCable is used, it needs to automatically reconnect with backoff. And, because we have "The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name," we also need to carefully examine `ActionCable.server.config.allow_same_origin_as_host` and `config.action_cable.allowed_request_origins`. We need to carefully consider the ActionCable forgery protection and how the requirement for "any host name" plays into that. The goal here is that websocket connections can be made from any host, but that this still offers proper security.

We've got to consider what happens when a player's connection drops and reconnects, or if they reload the page. How quickly do we detect disconnects? How quickly do we handle reconnects? We need near-instant updates, especially during tests. If a player in a QA test closes a tab, how long until the "Players" count updates? Do we rely on the WebSocket close frame, or a heartbeat timeout? Or will an HTTP/form submission without closing be the way to go?

What if the player joins via browser, loads the page, and the WebSocket immediately connects? Presence is registered immediately! Even better: if we consider the join POST and then wait for WS connect, that's almost immediate. Also, if there is a Turbo navigation, that needs to be taken into account. I should also investigate how `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest` (no JS) or navigation away from the join page will work.

So, let's get into the specifics of Rails 8.1, ActionCable, Turbo Streams, SSE, and presence. It's time to check which gems are installed and how those fit in with a robust solution.

require "rack"

module ActionCable
  module Server
    # # Action Cable Server Configuration
    #
    # An instance of this configuration object is available via
    # ActionCable.server.config, which allows you to tweak Action Cable
    # configuration in a Rails config initializer.
    class Configuration
      attr_accessor :logger, :log_tags
      attr_accessor :connection_class, :worker_pool_size
      attr_accessor :disable_request_forgery_protection, :allowed_request_origins, :allow_same_origin_as_host, :filter_parameters
      attr_accessor :cable, :url, :mount_path
      attr_accessor :precompile_assets
      attr_accessor :health_check_path, :health_check_application

      def initialize
        @log_tags = []

        @connection_class = -> { ActionCable::Connection::Base }
        @worker_pool_size = 4

        @disable_request_forgery_protection = false
        @allow_same_origin_as_host = true
        @filter_parameters = []

        @health_check_application = ->(env) {
          [200, { Rack::CONTENT_TYPE => "text/html", "date" => Time.now.httpdate }, []]
        }
      end

      # Returns constant of subscription adapter specified in config/cable.yml. If the
      # adapter cannot be found, this will default to the Redis adapter. Also makes
      # sure proper dependencies are required.
      def pubsub_adapter
        adapter = (cable.fetch("adapter") { "redis" })

        # Require the adapter itself and give useful feedback about
        #     1. Missing adapter gems and
        #     2. Adapter gems' missing dependencies.
        path_to_adapter = "action_cable/subscription_adapter/#{adapter}"
        begin
          require path_to_adapter
        rescue LoadError => e
          # We couldn't require the adapter itself. Raise an exception that points out
          # config typos and missing gems.
          if e.path == path_to_adapter
            # We can assume that a non-builtin adapter was specified, so it's either
            # misspelled or missing from Gemfile.
            raise e.class, "Could not load the '#{adapter}' Action Cable pubsub adapter. Ensure that the adapter is spelled correctly in config/cable.yml and that you've added the necessary adapter gem to your Gemfile.", e.backtrace

          # Bubbled up from the adapter require. Prefix the exception message with some
          # guidance about how to address it and reraise.
          else
            raise e.class, "Error loading the '#{adapter}' Action Cable pubsub adapter. Missing a gem it depends on? #{e.message}", e.backtrace
          end
        end

        adapter = adapter.camelize
        adapter = "PostgreSQL" if adapter == "Postgresql"
        "ActionCable::SubscriptionAdapter::#{adapter}".constantize
      end
    end
  end

Wait, this is smart. I'm pleased that ActionCable is leveraging `nio4r` for WebSockets. This is excellent! It's hijacking the socket and managing *all* WebSocket connections within an event loop. This means we're not tying up a Puma thread per WebSocket connection. That's a huge win in terms of scalability for ActionCable, particularly compared to SSE, where each client connection consumes a Puma thread. With SSE, just three players could potentially exhaust our 3-thread Puma server, leading to a deadlock.

Thank goodness we thought of this! Here's the advantage distilled:

*   ActionCable WebSockets with `nio4r` can handle many concurrent connections on a single-process Puma with limited threads.
*   SSE (using `ActionController::Live`) would be completely broken with only 3 Puma threads because it consumes one thread per open client connection.
*   Additionally, ActionCable's worker pool handles incoming/outgoing messages using a thread pool. And, we can also increase Puma's max threads (e.g., to `5` or `16`) and update `database.yml`'s `max_connections` to match, and enable SQLite WAL mode. module ActionCable
  module Server
    # # Action Cable Server Connections
    #
    # Collection class for all the connections that have been established on this
    # specific server. Remember, usually you'll run many Action Cable servers, so
    # you can't use this collection as a full list of all of the connections
    # established against your application. Instead, use RemoteConnections for that.
    module Connections # :nodoc:
      BEAT_INTERVAL = 3

      def connections
        @connections ||= []
      end

      def add_connection(connection)
        connections << connection
      end

      def remove_connection(connection)
        connections.delete connection
      end

      # WebSocket connection implementations differ on when they'll mark a connection
      # as stale. We basically never want a connection to go stale, as you then can't
      # rely on being able to communicate with the connection. To solve this, a 3
      # second heartbeat runs on all connections. If the beat fails, we automatically
      # disconnect.
      def setup_heartbeat_timer
        @heartbeat_timer ||= event_loop.timer(BEAT_INTERVAL) do
          event_loop.post { connections.each(&:beat) }
        end
      end

      def open_connections_statistics
        connections.map(&:statistics)
      end
    end
  end

        scheme = secure_request?(env) ? "wss:" : "ws:"

      end

      def self.secure_request?(env)
        return true if env["HTTPS"] == "on"
        return true if env["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_SSL"] == "on"
        return true if env["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_SCHEME"] == "https"
        return true if env["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO"] == "https"
        return true if env["rack.url_scheme"] == "https"

        false
      end

      CONNECTING = 0
      OPEN       = 1
      CLOSING    = 2
      CLOSED     = 3

      attr_reader :env, :url

      def initialize(env, event_target, event_loop, protocols)
        @env          = env
        @event_target = event_target
        @event_loop   = event_loop

        @driver = ::WebSocket::Driver.rack(self, protocols: protocols)

        @driver.on(:message) { |e| receive_message(e.data) }
        @driver.on(:close)   { |e| begin_close(e.reason, e.code) }
        @driver.on(:error)   { |e| emit_error(e.message) }

First, let's nail down how to track players *precisely*. ActionCable's *built-in* heartbeat is great (3-second interval), and ActionCable's client-side auto-reconnect is brilliant, but even with those safeguards, we must handle the edge cases. Half-open TCP connections, for example, where a server `write` succeeds, but the client vanishes without a `FIN`. Let's assume the server `beat` write *succeeds* on its end, for simplicity. If a client's Wi-Fi drops, we can't assume ActionCable will pick up the tab (due to the unreliable state of conference Wi-Fi!). So, we need to track active connections and make them *explicit* with a *periodic* client-side heartbeat/ping, so we can clean up stale connection entries. When a player subscribes, let's immediately register them in a memory store (`GamePresence`), broadcasting that count immediately to the moderator. Unsubscribing should *also* remove them, and broadcast.

Now, let's not make assumptions that a backgrounded tab is *necessarily* disconnected. We know background tabs throttle `setInterval`, which is a killer. And even worse, on iOS Safari, timers can be *suspended* when a phone's screen is off. Yikes! messages.thinking:
**Model Design and Implementation Plan**

Alright, let's get down to brass tacks. I need to get these models built out. I'm thinking: `Quiz`, `GamePresence`, `Game`, `GameQuestion`, `GameOption`, `Player`, and `Answer`.

I'm focusing particularly on the `Game` and `GamePresence` models, because they're the heart of this. I need to make sure everything's watertight, especially around state transitions and data integrity.

For `Game`, the game code will use a 32-character alphabet and is 5 chars long to ensure uniqueness and I'll include retries to handle collisions. The logic for starting a game from a quiz is pretty straightforward: load active questions, check for their presence, and create a `Game` record with the appropriate initial state ("lobby") and code. We'll create `GameQuestion` and `GameOption` records during the game creation.

The state transitions on `Game` are critical. I want to handle `start!`, `finish!`, `next_question!`, and `end_game!` with care. Each transition is going to need to be wrapped in a transaction to guarantee atomicity. I want to add in checks to ensure that the transition is valid given the current state and version. I need to add state versioning to prevent concurrency issues, and broadcast state changes after committing.

The `record_answer!` method is also important. I need to make sure that the game is in the correct state, that the question and option are valid, and then either find or create an `Answer` record. And, of course, broadcast the results, and handle concurrent answer submissions.

The next thing on my mind is how we serialize the game state, and I want to make *absolutely* sure that we're not leaking any information about the *correct* answer while the question is open. The `public_state` serializer is critical. When the question is open, I need to make sure the `correct` key is NEVER exposed in the JSON.  Only when the question is closed, I'll reveal the `correct` answer to the player. The `player_state_for` serializer needs to include the player's selected option and, critically, their outcome (correct, wrong, or none) only when the question is closed. I need to ensure that the `outcome` field is *not* present while the question is open. The `moderator_state` serializer needs to show answer counts and shares, but *not* leak the correct answer while the question is open.

Finally, I need to examine the `GamePresence` HTTP lease expiry mechanism. I need to ensure that there aren't any lingering background tasks or race conditions, particularly when the database is rolled back during tests. I'm going to set up a delayed check using `Concurrent::ScheduledTask` to prune expired leases. It should be robust.

require "set"
require "concurrent"

class GamePresence
  HTTP_LEASE_TTL = 7.0

  class << self
    def connect(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
      changed = false
      count = 0

      mutex.synchronize do
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        was_present = present_locked?(game_id, player_id)
        game_ws = ws_connections[game_id] ||= {}
        player_conns = game_ws[player_id] ||= Set.new
        player_conns.add(connection_id)
        http_leases[game_id]&.delete(player_id)
        changed = !was_present
        count = active_count_locked(game_id)
      end

      [ changed, count ]
    end

    def disconnect(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
      changed = false
      count = 0

      mutex.synchronize do
        if (game_ws = ws_connections[game_id])
          if (player_conns = game_ws[player_id])
            player_conns.delete(connection_id)
            game_ws.delete(player_id) if player_conns.empty?
          end
          ws_connections.delete(game_id) if game_ws.empty?
        end

        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        still_present = present_locked?(game_id, player_id)
        changed = !still_present
        count = active_count_locked(game_id)
      end

      [ changed, count ]
    end

    def touch_http(game_id, player_id, ttl: HTTP_LEASE_TTL)
      changed = false
      count = 0
      leased = false

      mutex.synchronize do
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        was_present = present_locked?(game_id, player_id)
        unless ws_connections.dig(game_id, player_id)&.any?
          (http_leases[game_id] ||= {})[player_id] = monotonic_now + ttl
          leased = true
        end
        changed = !was_present
        count = active_count_locked(game_id)
      end

      schedule_http_expiry_check(game_id, ttl) if leased

      [ changed, count ]
    end

    def active_count(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        active_count_locked(game_id)
      end
    end

    def active_player_ids(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        active_player_ids_locked(game_id)
      end
    end

    def prune_expired(game_id)
      pruned = false
      count = 0

      mutex.synchronize do
        before = active_count_locked(game_id)
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        count = active_count_locked(game_id)
        pruned = count != before
      end

      [ pruned, count ]
    end

    def clear_game(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        ws_connections.delete(game_id)
        http_leases.delete(game_id)
      end
    end

    def reset!
      mutex.synchronize do
        ws_connections.clear
        http_leases.clear
      end
    end

    private

    def mutex
      @mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def ws_connections
      @ws_connections ||= {}
    end

    def http_leases
      @http_leases ||= {}
    end

    def monotonic_now
      Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    end

    def prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
      leases = http_leases[game_id]
      return unless leases

      now = monotonic_now
      leases.delete_if { |_player_id, expires_at| expires_at <= now }
      http_leases.delete(game_id) if leases.empty?
    end

    def present_locked?(game_id, player_id)
      return true if ws_connections.dig(game_id, player_id)&.any?

      expires_at = http_leases.dig(game_id, player_id)
      expires_at.present? && expires_at > monotonic_now
    end

    def active_player_ids_locked(game_id)
      ids = Set.new
      ws_connections[game_id]&.each_key { |pid| ids.add(pid) }
      http_leases[game_id]&.each_key { |pid| ids.add(pid) }
      ids
    end

    def active_count_locked(game_id)
      active_player_ids_locked(game_id).size
    end

    def schedule_http_expiry_check(game_id, ttl)
      Concurrent::ScheduledTask.execute(ttl + 0.5) do
        pruned, _count = prune_expired(game_id)
        if pruned
          Rails.application.executor.wrap do
            Game.find_by(id: game_id)&.broadcast_moderator_counts!
          end
        end
      rescue StandardError
        nil
      end
    end
  end
end

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/game.rb
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  class NoActiveQuestionsError < StandardError; end

  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed ended].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789".chars.freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  def self.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    active = quiz.active_questions.to_a
    raise NoActiveQuestionsError, "Add or activate at least one question before starting a game." if active.empty?

    transaction do
      game = quiz.games.create!(code: generate_unique_code, status: "lobby")

      active.each_with_index do |question, q_index|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(
          source_question_id: question.id,
          body: question.body,
          position: q_index + 1
        )

        question.options.ordered.each_with_index do |option, o_index|
          game_question.game_options.create!(
            source_option_id: option.id,
            body: option.body,
            correct: option.correct?,
            position: o_index + 1
          )
        end
      end

      game
    end
  end

  def self.generate_unique_code
    loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.length)] }.join
      return candidate unless exists?(code: candidate)
    end
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def ended?
    status == "ended"
  end

  def ordered_game_questions
    game_questions.ordered.includes(:game_options)
  end

  def total_questions_count
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_game_question
    return nil if current_question_index.nil?

    game_questions.ordered.includes(:game_options).offset(current_question_index).first
  end

  def current_question_number
    return nil if current_question_index.nil?

    current_question_index + 1
  end

  def last_question?
    return false if current_question_index.nil?

    current_question_index >= total_questions_count - 1
  end

  def active_players_count
    GamePresence.active_count(id)
  end

  def current_answers_count
    question = current_game_question
    return 0 unless question

    question.answers.count
  end

  def start!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless lobby?
      next unless game_questions.exists?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "question_open",
        current_question_index: 0,
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        started_at: now,
        current_question_opened_at: now
      )
      current_game_question.update!(opened_at: now)
      transitioned = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if transitioned
    transitioned
  end

  def finish!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_open?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        state_version: state_version + 1
      )
      current_game_question&.update!(closed_at: now)
      transitioned = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if transitioned
    transitioned
  end

  def next_question!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_closed? && !last_question?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "question_open",
        current_question_index: current_question_index + 1,
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        current_question_opened_at: now
      )
      current_game_question.update!(opened_at: now)
      transitioned = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if transitioned
    transitioned
  end

  def end_game!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_closed? && last_question?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "ended",
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        ended_at: now
      )
      transitioned = true
    end

    broadcast_state! if transitioned
    transitioned
  end

  def record_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    saved_question_id = nil
    saved_option_id = nil

    transaction do
      reload
      next unless question_open?

      question = current_game_question
      next unless question && question.id == game_question_id.to_i

      option = question.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id.to_i)
      next unless option

      upsert_answer!(player: player, question: question, option: option)
      saved_question_id = question.id
      saved_option_id = option.id
    end

    if saved_option_id
      broadcast_moderator_counts!
      broadcast_player_answer!(player, saved_question_id, saved_option_id)
      { ok: true, game_question_id: saved_question_id, selected_option_id: saved_option_id }
    else
      { ok: false, state: player_state_for(player) }
    end
  end

  def moderator_state(join_url: nil)
    question = current_game_question
    total = total_questions_count
    answers_count = question ? question.answers.count : 0

    payload = {
      type: "state",
      status: status,
      state_version: state_version,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      active_players_count: active_players_count,
      answers_count: answers_count,
      question_number: current_question_number,
      total_questions: total,
      last_question: last_question?,
      question: nil
    }
    payload[:join_url] = join_url if join_url.present?

    if question && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      option_counts = question_closed? ? question.answers.group(:game_option_id).count : {}
      total_answers = option_counts.values.sum

      payload[:question] = {
        id: question.id,
        body: question.body,
        options: question.game_options.ordered.map do |opt|
          item = {
            id: opt.id,
            position: opt.position,
            body: opt.body
          }
          if question_closed?
            count = option_counts.fetch(opt.id, 0)
            item[:correct] = opt.correct?
            item[:count] = count
            item[:share] = total_answers.positive? ? ((count * 100.0) / total_answers).round(1) : 0
          end
          item
        end
      }
    end

    payload
  end

  def public_state
    question = current_game_question
    total = total_questions_count

    payload = {
      type: "state",
      status: status,
      state_version: state_version,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      question_number: current_question_number,
      total_questions: total,
      question: nil
    }

    if question && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      payload[:question] = {
        id: question.id,
        body: question.body,
        options: question.game_options.ordered.map do |opt|
          item = {
            id: opt.id,
            position: opt.position,
            body: opt.body
          }
          # Never reveal correct options before the question is closed.
          item[:correct] = opt.correct? if question_closed?
          item
        end
      }
    end

    payload
  end

  def player_state_for(player)
    state = public_state.merge(
      player_name: player.name,
      selected_option_id: nil
    )

    question = current_game_question
    if question && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      selected_option_id = Answer.where(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: question.id).pick(:game_option_id)
      state[:selected_option_id] = selected_option_id

      if question_closed?
        state[:outcome] =
          if selected_option_id.nil?
            "none"
          elsif question.game_options.any? { |opt| opt.id == selected_option_id && opt.correct? }
            "correct"
          else
            "wrong"
          end
      end
    end

    state
  end

  def moderator_stream_name
    "game_moderator:#{id}"
  end

  def public_stream_name
    "game_public:#{id}"
  end

  def player_stream_name(player)
    "game_player:#{id}:#{player.id}"
  end

  def broadcast_state!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, moderator_state)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(public_stream_name, public_state)
  end

  def broadcast_moderator_counts!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      moderator_stream_name,
      {
        type: "counts",
        state_version: state_version,
        active_players_count: active_players_count,
        answers_count: current_answers_count
      }
    )
  end

  def broadcast_player_answer!(player, game_question_id, game_option_id)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      player_stream_name(player),
      {
        type: "player_answer",
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        selected_option_id: game_option_id
      }
    )
  end

  private

  def version_mismatch?(expected_version)
    expected_version.present? && state_version != expected_version.to_i
  end

  def upsert_answer!(player:, question:, option:)
    now = Time.current
    answer = Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: question.id)
    answer.game_id = id
    answer.game_option_id = option.id
    answer.answered_at = now
    answer.save!
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    existing = Answer.find_by!(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: question.id)
    existing.update!(game_option_id: option.id, answered_at: now)
  end
end
EOF

class GamePlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    @player = Player.find_signed(params[:token], purpose: :player_stream)
    return reject unless @game && @player && @player.game_id == @game.id

    @presence_connection_id = SecureRandom.hex(8)

    stream_from @game.public_stream_name
    stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player)

    @presence_registered = true
    changed, _count = GamePresence.connect(@game.id, @player.id, @presence_connection_id)
    @game.reload
    @game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if changed

    transmit @game.player_state_for(@player)
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @presence_registered && @game && @player

    @presence_registered = false
    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect(@game.id, @player.id, @presence_connection_id)
    if changed
      Game.find_by(id: @game.id)&.broadcast_moderator_counts!
    end
  end
end

class PlaysController < ApplicationController
  CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE = :quizzy_client_token

  before_action :set_game
  before_action :disable_caching

  def show
    @player = current_player_for(@game)

    if @player
      @state = @game.player_state_for(@player)
      @player_stream_token = @player.signed_id(purpose: :player_stream, expires_in: 24.hours)
      render :show
    elsif @game.ended?
      render :ended
    else
      @player = @game.players.build
      render :join
    end
  end

  def join
    if @game.ended?
      return render :ended, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end

    if current_player_for(@game)
      return redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    end

    token = ensure_client_token
    @player = @game.players.build(name: params.dig(:player, :name), client_token: token)

    if @game.reload.ended?
      return render :ended, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end

    if @player.save
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      render :join, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
  end

  def answer
    @player = current_player_for(@game)
    unless @player
      return respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: { error: "Join the game first" }, status: :unauthorized }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    end

    result = @game.record_answer!(
      player: @player,
      game_question_id: params[:game_question_id],
      game_option_id: params[:game_option_id]
    )

    if result[:ok]
      respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: result, status: :ok }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    else
      respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: result[:state], status: :conflict }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    end
  end

  def state
    @player = current_player_for(@game)

    if @player
      if params[:fallback] == "1"
        changed, _count = GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if changed
      end
      render json: @game.player_state_for(@player)
    else
      render json: @game.public_state
    end
  end

  private

  def set_game
    @game = Game.find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
  end

  def disable_caching
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
  end

  def current_client_token
    cookies.signed[CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE].presence
  end

  def ensure_client_token
    existing = current_client_token
    return existing if existing

    token = SecureRandom.hex(24)
    cookies.signed[CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE] = {
      value: token,
      httponly: true,
      same_site: :lax,
      expires: 1.year.from_now
    }
    token
  end

  def current_player_for(game)
    token = current_client_token
    return nil unless token

    game.players.find_by(client_token: token)
  end
end
EOF

**Comprehensive Test Plan for Robust Application Behavior**

Okay, so I've just seen that the Brakeman and RuboCop checks are clean - good start! Now it's time to dive deep and ensure this application is truly bulletproof. I need to design a test suite that leaves no stone unturned, especially considering the real-time, interactive nature of the application. I'm going to focus on:

1.  **Model Integrity:** First, I'll rigorously test the core logic of the game, including how questions are started, skipped, and managed throughout the game lifecycle. Specifically, I'll confirm that question editing or deletion doesn't mess with active games and that quiz exports remain clean and accurate, without any game or player state leakage. I'll thoroughly test state transitions, ensuring that unexpected actions are handled gracefully to prevent game corruption. And, crucially, I need to confirm the presence of player deduplication across different connections, along with the correct handling of game states in public and player-specific contexts. I also need to make sure answers are processed as designed.

2.  **Controller & Security:** Next up, controllers, authentication, and security are going to be tested for moderator access, player participation, and secure data handling. I'll test basic auth requirements, join form validation, and ensure that joining a game sets the proper signed cookie, preventing unwanted access. During a question, I'll *explicitly* inspect the raw HTTP responses, confirming that no hint of the correct answer leaks in the HTML or JSON to players. I'll verify the handling of various invalid inputs and edge cases, such as an attempt to answer after a game has ended. I need to make sure that the player's information remains secure.

3.  **Channel Operations:** I'll dive into ensuring that the channel logic functions correctly, confirming that invalid tokens are rejected, valid moderator tokens are accepted and the correct streaming and state data are transmitted. The same is true for player and public channels. I need to make sure that each channel streams the correct data.

4.  **Multi-Browser System Testing:** This is where things get really interesting. I'll simulate real-world usage using multiple isolated Chromium browser sessions to run several full-blown scenarios, including:

    *   **Full End-to-End Game:** I need to make sure that the game runs without a hitch with multiple players, including those joining late or dropping off. I'll be meticulously checking every state transition, answer submission, and moderator action, making sure there are *zero* page reloads. I need to confirm that join links and QR codes render correctly and encode the correct URL. I'm going to be checking security by inspecting HTML source code, ensuring that the players don't have access to the answer.
    *   **Multiple Games:** It's important to make sure that multiple games of the same quiz don't interfere with each other, that player's browsers remain isolated for different sessions and that player progress is not shared between games.
    *   **Resilience:** I need to simulate network interruptions (think conference Wi-Fi) by dropping WebSocket connections and making sure the application gracefully recovers, so that, upon reconnection, players are immediately brought up-to-date with the current game state, without getting stuck.

In summary, this is an exhaustive test plan. I'm aiming for not just passing tests, but absolute confidence in the application's stability, security, and real-time behavior.

require "test_helper"

class GameTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def build_quiz_with_questions
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Conference Quiz")

    q1 = quiz.questions.build(body: "First active?", active: true)
    q1.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Wrong A", correct: false },
      { body: "Right B", correct: true }
    ])

    q2 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Inactive skipped?", active: false)
    q2.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Skip 1", correct: true },
      { body: "Skip 2", correct: false }
    ])

    q3 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Second active (multi)?", active: true)
    q3.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Right 1", correct: true },
      { body: "Right 2", correct: true },
      { body: "Wrong 3", correct: false }
    ])

    quiz
  end

  test "start_for_quiz! snapshots active questions and skips inactive ones" do
    quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)

    assert_equal "lobby", game.status
    assert_match(/\A[A-Z2-9]{5}\z/, game.code)
    assert_equal 2, game.game_questions.count
    assert_equal [ "First active?", "Second active (multi)?" ], game.game_questions.ordered.pluck(:body)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], game.game_questions.ordered.pluck(:position)
  end

  test "start_for_quiz! raises NoActiveQuestionsError when quiz has no active questions" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Empty Quiz")
    assert_raises(Game::NoActiveQuestionsError) do
      Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    end
  end

  test "editing or deleting source quiz questions does not affect an existing game" do
    quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    game.start!

    # Modify and delete original questions on the quiz
    q1 = quiz.questions.ordered.first
    q1.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Changed Option 1", correct: true },
      { body: "Changed Option 2", correct: false }
    ])
    quiz.questions.ordered.last.destroy!

    game.reload
    assert_equal 2, game.game_questions.count
    assert_equal [ "Wrong A", "Right B" ], game.current_game_question.game_options.ordered.pluck(:body)
  end

  test "destroying a quiz cascades cleanly through games, players, and answers" do
    quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    player = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-1")
    game.start!
    q = game.current_game_question
    game.record_answer!(player: player, game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: q.game_options.first.id)

    assert_equal 1, Game.count
    assert_equal 1, Player.count
    assert_equal 1, Answer.count

    quiz.destroy!

    assert_equal 0, Quiz.count
    assert_equal 0, Game.count
    assert_equal 0, GameQuestion.count
    assert_equal 0, GameOption.count
    assert_equal 0, Player.count
    assert_equal 0, Answer.count
  end

  test "quiz export format stays strictly title and questions even after games are played" do
    quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-1")
    game.start!

    exported = Quiz::Exporter.new(quiz).as_json
    assert_equal %w[title questions], exported.keys
    assert_equal 3, exported["questions"].size
  end

  test "state transitions respect order and expected_version guard" do
    quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)

    # Cannot finish or next from lobby
    assert_not game.finish!
    assert_not game.next_question!
    assert_not game.end_game!

    # Wrong expected_version does nothing
    assert_not game.start!(expected_version: 99)
    assert game.lobby?

    assert game.start!(expected_version: 0)
    assert game.question_open?
    assert_equal 1, game.current_question_number
    assert_not game.last_question?

    # Cannot next or end while question is open
    assert_not game.next_question!
    assert_not game.end_game!

    assert game.finish!(expected_version: game.state_version)
    assert game.question_closed?
    assert_not game.end_game! # Not last question yet

    # Double-click guard: stale version fails
    stale = game.state_version
    assert game.next_question!(expected_version: stale)
    assert_not game.next_question!(expected_version: stale)

    assert game.question_open?
    assert_equal 2, game.current_question_number
    assert game.last_question?

    assert game.finish!
    assert_not game.next_question! # Last question cannot next
    assert game.end_game!
    assert game.ended?
  end

  test "public_state and player_state_for never leak correct answers while question is open" do
    quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    player = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-1")
    game.start!

    pub = game.public_state
    pstate = game.player_state_for(player)

    assert_not pub.to_json.downcase.include?("correct")
    assert_not pstate.to_json.downcase.include?("correct")
    assert_not pstate.key?(:outcome)

    # Pick wrong option first, then change to right option
    q = game.current_game_question
    wrong_opt = q.game_options.find_by!(correct: false)
    right_opt = q.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)

    res1 = game.record_answer!(player: player, game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: wrong_opt.id)
    assert res1[:ok]
    assert_equal 1, game.current_answers_count

    res2 = game.record_answer!(player: player, game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: right_opt.id)
    assert res2[:ok]
    assert_equal 1, game.current_answers_count # Still 1 player who answered

    # Still no leak after answering
    assert_not game.player_state_for(player).to_json.downcase.include?("correct")

    # Finish reveals correct options and outcome
    game.finish!
    closed_state = game.player_state_for(player)
    assert_equal "correct", closed_state[:outcome]
    assert_equal right_opt.id, closed_state[:selected_option_id]
    assert_equal true, closed_state[:question][:options].find { |o| o[:id] == right_opt.id }[:correct]

    # Answering after close is rejected
    late = game.record_answer!(player: player, game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: wrong_opt.id)
    assert_not late[:ok]
    assert_equal right_opt.id, Answer.find_by!(player: player, game_question: q).game_option_id
  end

  test "GamePresence deduplicates multiple connections per player and tracks HTTP leases" do
    changed, count = GamePresence.connect(1, 10, "conn-a")
    assert changed
    assert_equal 1, count

    # Second tab for same player does not double-count
    changed, count = GamePresence.connect(1, 10, "conn-b")
    assert_not changed
    assert_equal 1, count

    # Second player increments count
    changed, count = GamePresence.connect(1, 20, "conn-c")
    assert changed
    assert_equal 2, count

    # Closing first tab of player 10 keeps them present
    changed, count = GamePresence.disconnect(1, 10, "conn-a")
    assert_not changed
    assert_equal 2, count

    # Closing second tab of player 10 removes them
    changed, count = GamePresence.disconnect(1, 10, "conn-b")
    assert changed
    assert_equal 1, count

    # Different game is isolated
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(2)

    # HTTP fallback lease works and is replaced when WS connects
    changed, count = GamePresence.touch_http(1, 30, ttl: 5.0)
    assert changed
    assert_equal 2, count

    changed, count = GamePresence.connect(1, 30, "conn-d")
    assert_not changed
    assert_equal 2, count
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class LiveGameTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  def create_quiz_with_active_question
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "HTTP Live Quiz")
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: "Capital of France?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Berlin", correct: false },
      { body: "Paris", correct: true }
    ])
    quiz

  test "moderator game endpoints require HTTP Basic auth" do
    quiz = create_quiz_with_active_question
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)

    post moderate_quiz_games_path(quiz)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    get moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    get state_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    post start_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    post finish_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    post next_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized

    post end_moderate_game_path(game)
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "creating a game with no active questions redirects back with alert" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "No Active Questions")
    post moderate_quiz_games_path(quiz), headers: basic_auth_headers
    assert_redirected_to moderate_quiz_path(quiz)
    assert_equal 0, Game.count
  end

  test "player endpoints are public, remember player per game, and never leak correct answer while open" do
    quiz = create_quiz_with_active_question
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)

    # Join page works without auth (case-insensitive code)
    get play_path(game.code.downcase)
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Your name"
    assert_includes response.body, "Join"

    # Blank name rejected
    post join_play_path(game.code), params: { player: { name: "   " } }
    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal 0, game.players.count

    # Valid join remembers player via signed cookie
    post join_play_path(game.code), params: { player: { name: "Alice" } }
    assert_redirected_to play_path(game.code)
    follow_redirect!
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Hi, Alice!"

    # Opening join link again in same browser continues as Alice
    get play_path(game.code)
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Hi, Alice!"
    assert_not_includes response.body, "Your name"

    # Start question as moderator
    post start_moderate_game_path(game), headers: basic_auth_headers, as: :json
    assert_response :success

    # Player HTML and JSON state MUST NOT leak correct answer while open
    get play_path(game.code)
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Capital of France?"
    assert_not_includes response.body.downcase, "correct"

    get state_play_path(game.code), as: :json
    assert_response :success
    assert_not_includes response.body.downcase, "correct"

    # Submit answer
    q = game.current_game_question
    paris = q.game_options.find_by!(body: "Paris")
    berlin = q.game_options.find_by!(body: "Berlin")

    post answer_play_path(game.code),
         params: { game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: paris.id },
         as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    # Finish question
    post finish_moderate_game_path(game), headers: basic_auth_headers, as: :json
    assert_response :success

    # Changing answer after finish is rejected with 409 Conflict
    post answer_play_path(game.code),
         params: { game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: berlin.id },
         as: :json
    assert_response :conflict
    assert_equal "correct", response.parsed_body["outcome"]

    # End quiz
    post end_moderate_game_path(game), headers: basic_auth_headers, as: :json
    assert_response :success

    # New browser cannot join after end
    open_session do |late_visitor|
      late_visitor.get play_path(game.code)
      assert_equal 200, late_visitor.response.status
      assert_includes late_visitor.response.body, "The quiz is over"
      assert_not_includes late_visitor.response.body, "Your name"

    # Second game of same quiz asks same browser for name again

    get play_path(game2.code)
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Your name"
    assert_includes response.body, "Join"
  end

  test "invalid game code returns 404" do
    get play_path("ZZZZZ")
    assert_response :not_found
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class GameChannelsTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  def create_game
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Channel Quiz")
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: "2 + 2?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "3", correct: false },
      { body: "4", correct: true }
    ])
    Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
  end

  test "GameModeratorChannel requires valid signed token and transmits state" do
    @channel_class = GameModeratorChannel
    game = create_game

    subscribe(token: "invalid-token")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    token = game.signed_id(purpose: :moderator_stream)
    subscribe(token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.moderator_stream_name
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end

  test "GamePlayerChannel tracks presence and transmits safe player state" do
    @channel_class = GamePlayerChannel
    game = create_game
    player = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-a")
    game.start!

    # Rejected with invalid token
    subscribe(code: game.code, token: "bad")
    assert subscription.rejected?
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)

    token = player.signed_id(purpose: :player_stream)
    subscribe(code: game.code, token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.public_stream_name
    assert_has_stream game.player_stream_name(player)
    assert_equal 1, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)

    # Transmitted state while open does NOT leak correct answer
    payload = transmissions.last
    assert_equal "question_open", payload[:status]
    assert_not payload.to_json.downcase.include?("correct")

    unsubscribe
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)
  end

  test "GamePublicChannel streams status without counting as active player" do
    @channel_class = GamePublicChannel
    game = create_game

    subscribe(code: game.code)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.public_stream_name
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end
end

require "test_helper"

module GameChannelTestHelper
  def create_game
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Channel Quiz")
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: "2 + 2?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "3", correct: false },
      { body: "4", correct: true }
    ])
    Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
  end
end

class GameModeratorChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GameModeratorChannel

  test "requires valid signed token and transmits state" do
    game = create_game

    subscribe(token: "invalid-token")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    token = game.signed_id(purpose: :moderator_stream)
    subscribe(token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.moderator_stream_name
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end
end

class GamePlayerChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GamePlayerChannel

  test "tracks presence and transmits safe player state" do
    game = create_game
    player = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-a")
    game.start!

    subscribe(code: game.code, token: "bad")
    assert subscription.rejected?
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)

    token = player.signed_id(purpose: :player_stream)
    subscribe(code: game.code, token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.public_stream_name
    assert_has_stream game.player_stream_name(player)
    assert_equal 1, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)

    payload = transmissions.last
    assert_equal "question_open", payload[:status]
    assert_not payload.to_json.downcase.include?("correct")

    unsubscribe
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)
  end
end

class GamePublicChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GamePublicChannel

  test "streams status without counting as active player" do
    game = create_game

    subscribe(code: game.code)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.public_stream_name
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.active_count(game.id)
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
  end
end

require "application_system_test_case"

class LiveGameTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  def create_conference_quiz
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Ruby Conf Live")

    q1 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?", active: true)
    q1.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "418", correct: false },
      { body: "429", correct: true },
      { body: "503", correct: false }
    ])

    q2 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Inactive question that must be skipped", active: false)
    q2.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Skip A", correct: true },
      { body: "Skip B", correct: false }
    ])

    q3 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Which protocols run over TCP?", active: true)
    q3.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "HTTP/1.1", correct: true },
      { body: "WebSocket", correct: true },
      { body: "UDP", correct: false }
    ])

    q4 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Final question: 6 * 7?", active: true)
    q4.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "41", correct: false },
      { body: "42", correct: true }
    ])

    quiz
  end

  test "full live game with multiple players, live counters, answer changes, disconnects, late joiner, and no reloads" do
    quiz = create_conference_quiz
    join_url = nil
    game = nil

    # Moderator starts a game from the quiz page
    using_session(:moderator) do
      authenticate_as_moderator
      visit moderate_quiz_path(quiz)
      assert_selector "h1", text: "Ruby Conf Live"

      click_button "Start a game"
      assert_match %r{\A/moderate/games/\d+\z}, current_path

      game = Game.last
      assert_selector "h1", text: "Ruby Conf Live"

      join_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip
      assert_includes join_url, "/play/#{game.code}"
      assert_match %r{\Ahttp://.+?/play/#{game.code}\z}, join_url

      # Verify QR code SVG is rendered with visible size and matches the exact join link
      assert_selector ".qr svg path"
      svg_dims = evaluate_script("(() => { const r = document.querySelector('.qr svg').getBoundingClientRect(); return [r.width, r.height]; })()")
      assert_operator svg_dims[0], :>, 50
      assert_operator svg_dims[1], :>, 50

      expected_qr = RQRCode::QRCode.new(join_url, level: :m)
      expected_path_d = Nokogiri::XML(expected_qr.as_svg(module_size: 8, offset: 32, standalone: true, use_path: true)).at_css("path")["d"]
      actual_path_d = evaluate_script("document.querySelector('.qr svg path').getAttribute('d')")
      assert_equal expected_path_d, actual_path_d

      # Verify exact visible text with no newline splitting "Players: 0"
      assert_text "Players: 0"
      assert_includes evaluate_script("document.body.innerText"), "Players: 0"
      assert_button "Start"
    end

    # Player 1 (Alice) opens join link, tests blank validation, then joins
    using_session(:alice) do
      visit join_url
      assert_field "Your name"
      assert_button "Join"

      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Name can't be blank"

      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
    end

    # Moderator sees Players: 1 LIVE without page reload
    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Players: 1"
    end

    # Player 2 (Bob) joins
    using_session(:bob) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Bob!"
    end

    # Moderator sees Players: 2 LIVE without page reload
    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Players: 2"
      assert_includes evaluate_script("document.body.innerText"), "Players: 2"
    end

    # Bob leaves the page -> active players counter drops to 1 LIVE
    using_session(:bob) do
      visit "/"
    end

    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Players: 1"
    end

    # Bob opens join link again in same browser -> remembered automatically, back to Players: 2
    using_session(:bob) do
      visit join_url
      assert_text "Hi, Bob!"
      assert_no_field "Your name"
      assert_no_button "Join"
    end

    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Players: 2"

      # Moderator clicks Start -> Question 1 of 3 opens
      click_button "Start"
      assert_text "Question 1 of 3"
      assert_text "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?"
      assert_text "418"
      assert_text "429"
      assert_text "503"
      assert_text "Answers: 0 / 2"
      assert_includes evaluate_script("document.body.innerText"), "Answers: 0 / 2"
      assert_button "Finish"
      assert_no_text "Correct"
    end

    # Alice receives Question 1 LIVE without reload; verify NO correct answer leak in page source!
    using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?"
      assert_button "418"
      assert_button "429"
      assert_button "503"
      assert_not_includes page.html.downcase, "correct"

      # Alice taps wrong answer first -> marked "Your answer"
      click_button "418"
      within("button.play-option", text: "418") do

      end
      within("button.play-option", text: "429") do
        assert_no_text "Your answer"
      end
    end

    # Moderator sees Answers: 1 / 2 LIVE
    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    # Alice changes her mind to 429 -> last pick counts, still 1 / 2
    using_session(:alice) do
      click_button "429"
      within("button.play-option", text: "429") do
        assert_text "Your answer"
      end
      within("button.play-option", text: "418") do
        assert_no_text "Your answer"
      end
    end

    # Bob temporarily leaves -> active players drops so counter shows 1 / 1 LIVE
    using_session(:bob) do
      assert_text "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?"
      visit "/"
    end

    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1"
    end

    # Bob returns (remembered!) and picks wrong answer 503
    using_session(:bob) do
      visit join_url
      assert_text "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?"
      click_button "503"
      within("button.play-option", text: "503") do
        assert_text "Your answer"
      end
    end

    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Answers: 2 / 2"

      # Finish Question 1 -> shows answer count for each option + marks correct option with "Correct" + Next button
      click_button "Finish"
      assert_button "Next"
      assert_no_button "End quiz"

      within("ol.stage-options > li", text: "418") do
        assert_selector ".stage-option__count", text: "0"
        assert_no_text "Correct"
      end
      within("ol.stage-options > li", text: "429") do
        assert_selector ".stage-option__count", text: "1"
        assert_text "Correct"
      end
      within("ol.stage-options > li", text: "503") do
        assert_selector ".stage-option__count", text: "1"
        assert_no_text "Correct"
      end
    end

    # Alice sees "Correct!" LIVE, Bob sees "Wrong!" LIVE (and NOT "Correct!")
    using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Correct!"
      assert_selector "button.play-option[disabled]", count: 3
    end

    using_session(:bob) do
      assert_text "Wrong!"
      assert_no_text "Correct"
    end

    # Moderator clicks Next -> skips inactive Q2, opens Q3 as "Question 2 of 3"
    using_session(:moderator) do
      click_button "Next"
      assert_text "Question 2 of 3"
      assert_text "Which protocols run over TCP?"
      assert_no_text "Inactive question that must be skipped"
      assert_text "Answers: 0 / 2"
    end

    # Late joiner Charlie joins mid-game during Q2!
    using_session(:charlie) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Charlie"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Which protocols run over TCP?"
    end

    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Answers: 0 / 3"
    end

    # Alice picks HTTP/1.1 (correct), Bob picks WebSocket (also correct), Charlie does not answer
    using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Which protocols run over TCP?"
      click_button "HTTP/1.1"
    end
    using_session(:bob) do
      assert_text "Which protocols run over TCP?"
      click_button "WebSocket"
    end

    using_session(:moderator) do
      assert_text "Answers: 2 / 3"

      within("ol.stage-options > li", text: "HTTP/1.1") do

        assert_selector ".stage-option__count", text: "1"
      end
      within("ol.stage-options > li", text: "WebSocket") do
        assert_text "Correct"
        assert_selector ".stage-option__count", text: "1"
      end
      within("ol.stage-options > li", text: "UDP") do
        assert_no_text "Correct"
        assert_selector ".stage-option__count", text: "0"
      end
    end

    using_session(:alice) { assert_text "Correct!" }
    using_session(:bob) { assert_text "Correct!" }
    using_session(:charlie) do
      assert_text "No answer"
      assert_no_text "Correct!"
      assert_no_text "Wrong!"
    end

    # Unjoined visitor opens join link right before end
    using_session(:latecomer) do
      visit join_url
      assert_field "Your name"
      assert_button "Join"
    end

    # Moderator moves to last question ("Question 3 of 3")
    using_session(:moderator) do
      click_button "Next"
      assert_text "Question 3 of 3"
      assert_text "Final question: 6 * 7?"

    using_session(:alice) { assert_text "No answer" }
